built.label: the taxonomy -- Tier K and what it obliges
built.text: **Tier K — Keystone-certified.** A document whose load-bearing claims are backed by a **machine-checked kernel terminal at a pin**, Gate-1-graded (DERIVES, or INTERFACES-with-a-named-premise). *Obligation:* every such claim states its **grade · terminal · pin**, and the axiom profile is written in full ("the standard three axioms {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}", or cleaner). *Citation rule:* **may be cited as certification** — the terminal, at its grade, is the warrant.

built.label: the taxonomy -- Tier C, which certifies nothing
built.text: **Tier C — Cluster-synthesis.** A document that **organizes** certified results into a cross-system picture, panel, map, or interpretation — asserting *relationships* not individually certified. *Obligation:* state the invariant it organizes on; flag any tuple/value that is a **coordinate, not an invariant**; carry the Gate-1b discipline (classification × certification is the invariant, not a shared tuple). *Citation rule:* **cite for orientation and organization — NEVER as certification of the relationships it draws.** This is the taxonomy's load-bearing rule.
